## What changed
- **`.github/workflows/shiki-mergegate.yml`** — "Prepare PR context" now builds the base `.shiki` snapshot (`git archive origin/<base_ref>`, reusing the existing fetch). "MergeGate metadata check" resolves the merged-PR proof the same way the CCA workflow does (task id → base snapshot `expected_pr` → `gh pr view` MERGED gate) and passes `--base-shiki` + `--merged-prs` to `mergegate_check.py`. So a `post_merge_reconcile` PR can pass instead of blocking on a missing base snapshot. All context flows through `env:` — no `${{ }}` in run bodies.
- **`.github/workflows/shiki-orchestrator.yml`** — comment/input-derived values (`EVENT_NAME`, `INPUT_PLAN_PATH`, `INPUT_MODE`, `MODE`, `PLAN_PATH`, `RUN_ID`) now flow through `env:` and are referenced as quoted shell vars, closing the expression-injection surface. The commit-evidence guard stages `.shiki` first, then guards on `git diff --cached --quiet`, so new untracked evidence is committed+pushed instead of silently dropped.
- **`scripts/validate_shiki.py`** — new `validate_workflow_invocation_contracts()` (wired into `main()`) asserts the metadata job invokes `mergegate_check.py` with `--base-shiki` and `--merged-prs`, and that the two hardened workflows carry no `${{ }}` inside any `run:` body.
- **`tests/test_workflow_invocation.py`** (new) + **`scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh`** — the TDD coverage and contract-string assertions.

- Passing `--base-shiki` to the metadata check also activates `enforce_untrusted_shiki_mutations`' protected-base comparison for normal PRs. This is consistent with — not new relative to — the authoritative "MergeGate policy check" (shiki-cca-completion.yml), which already passes `--base-shiki` on every PR, so it strengthens the metadata check without newly blocking legitimate PRs.
